violation_type: AI-generated non-consensual intimate imagery
outcome: First civil complaint filed under DEFIANCE Act; case pending
summary: First known civil lawsuit filed under the DEFIANCE Act for AI-generated non-consensual intimate imagery. Details sealed at plaintiff's request; case established standing and jurisdiction precedent.

violation_type: Using EU member data for AI training without consent; unclear opt-out mechanism
outcome: Order to stop processing French users' data for AI training; formal warning
summary: CNIL ordered LinkedIn to stop using French users' data for AI model training, finding that LinkedIn's opt-out mechanism was inadequate and did not constitute valid consent under GDPR. LinkedIn complied within 2 weeks.

violation_type: Unlawful processing of Google account data for Bard AI training
outcome: Warning + corrective order
summary: Dutch DPA found Google processed personal data from Google accounts to train Bard (now Gemini) without adequate legal basis or transparency; issued warning and corrective order. Fine assessment pending.

violation_type: Using EU users' personal data to train Grok AI without valid legal basis
outcome: Interim injunction from Irish High Court requiring X to stop processing EU user data for AI training; X agreed to comply
summary: Irish DPC secured High Court injunction requiring X to halt using EU users' public posts to train Grok AI models. X agreed to stop pending full investigation. Landmark precedent on AI training data and GDPR consent.

violation_type: AEDT used without completed bias audit; audit results not posted publicly
outcome: Warning letters; compliance orders; voluntary corrective action
summary: NYC DCWP issued warning letters and compliance orders to multiple employers using Eightfold AI's automated hiring platform for failing to complete the required annual bias audit before deployment and for not publicly posting audit results as required by Local Law 144.

violation_type: Unlawful data processing for AI training; no age verification; inaccurate outputs
outcome: Fine — €15 million ($15.3M)
summary: Italian DPA fined OpenAI €15 million for: collecting personal data to train ChatGPT without valid legal basis, failing to verify user ages, and generating false information about real individuals. OpenAI also required to run an information campaign.

violation_type: Reckless facial recognition deployment in stores causing discriminatory misidentifications
outcome: 5-year ban on using facial recognition in retail stores
summary: FTC banned Rite Aid from using AI facial recognition in retail stores for 5 years after finding it deployed the technology recklessly, leading to false positives disproportionately affecting Black, Asian, and Latino customers who were wrongly accused of shoplifting. The first FTC ban on biometric AI use.

violation_type: GenAI features without required security assessment and labeling
outcome: Mandatory suspension of GenAI features pending compliance
summary: CAC required Weibo to suspend several generative AI features that had launched without completing the mandatory security assessment filing under the GenAI Interim Measures. Features restored after compliance filing.

enforcement_body: NYC Department of Consumer and Worker Protection (DCWP)
violation_type: Using AEDT without required bias audit or notice to candidates
outcome: First enforcement notice under NYC LL144; compliance order
summary: NYC DCWP issued the first enforcement notice under Local Law 144 to Tandym Group for using an automated employment decision tool without completing the required annual bias audit and providing required candidate notice. No monetary penalty announced in first action.

violation_type: Retaining children's voice data and location data for AI training against parents' deletion requests
outcome: Civil penalty + compliance order
summary: $25 million civil penalty for violating COPPA and FTC Act by retaining children's Alexa voice recordings for AI training even after parents requested deletion. Amazon required to delete data and prohibited from training AI on unlawfully retained data.

violation_type: Allowing employees and contractors to access users' private video footage; inadequate security for AI surveillance data
outcome: Civil penalty $5.8M + comprehensive security program + prohibition on using data for AI training
summary: $5.8 million civil penalty against Amazon's Ring subsidiary for allowing employees and contractors to access private customers' camera footage without consent, including for training AI models. Ring was prohibited from using any unlawfully accessed customer data for AI product development.

violation_type: Unlawful data transfers to US; inadequate legal basis for personalised advertising
outcome: Fine + order to suspend data transfers within 5 months
summary: €1.2 billion ($1.3B) fine for transferring EU users' personal data to US servers without adequate safeguards following Schrems II ruling. Largest GDPR fine ever issued. Meta appealed.

violation_type: Unlawful processing of children's data including algorithmic personalisation
outcome: Fine — £12.7 million ($16.9M)
summary: UK ICO fined TikTok £12.7 million for unlawfully processing the personal data of approximately 1.4 million under-13s without parental consent, and for failing to verify user ages when its algorithm personalised content for children.

violation_type: Unlawful processing of French residents' biometric data; failure to respond to access requests
outcome: Fine — €20 million ($21M) + order to delete data
summary: CNIL fined Clearview AI €20 million for collecting facial images of French residents without legal basis, failing to honour deletion requests, and building a biometric database covering hundreds of thousands of French individuals.

violation_type: Collecting facial geometry from Illinois users via Google Photos without BIPA consent
outcome: Settlement — $100 million
summary: $100 million BIPA class settlement for Google Photos facial recognition grouping feature that collected biometric data from Illinois users without written consent or data retention policy.

violation_type: Algorithm recommendations promoting harmful content; failure to register algorithm
outcome: Fine + mandatory algorithm registration; content review system upgrade
summary: CAC sanctioned ByteDance's Toutiao platform for algorithm recommendations promoting excessively negative social content and failure to register recommendation algorithm as required. First major enforcement under Algorithm Recommendation Provisions.

violation_type: Processing children's personal data including for algorithmic content targeting
outcome: Fine — €405 million ($415M)
summary: Irish DPC fined Meta's Instagram €405 million for exposing children's email addresses and phone numbers through business account defaults and processing children's data for algorithmic advertising without valid legal basis. The largest children's privacy GDPR fine at the time.

violation_type: Biometric data collection without consent
outcome: Settlement
summary: Class action alleging collection of voiceprints without BIPA consent; settled for $900,000.

violation_type: Unlawful scraping of facial images of UK residents without consent or legal basis
outcome: Fine — £7.5 million ($9.4M) + order to delete UK data
summary: ICO fined Clearview AI £7.5 million for unlawfully collecting facial images of UK residents from the internet to build a facial recognition database, finding no lawful basis under UK GDPR. Clearview was ordered to delete all UK individuals' data from its database and prohibited from further processing.

violation_type: Scraping and selling facial recognition database without consent
outcome: Injunction — Clearview permanently banned from selling access to Illinois residents' data
summary: Settlement permanently banning Clearview AI from selling access to its facial recognition database to private entities in the US and from adding new Illinois residents to its database without consent. The most significant BIPA injunctive outcome to date.

violation_type: Facial recognition data collection without consent
outcome: Settlement
summary: Class action alleging BIPA violations for facial recognition and voice data collection in Illinois; settled for $92 million — largest BIPA settlement at the time.

violation_type: Advertising targeting system — unlawful processing of personal data
outcome: Fine
summary: €746 million ($886M) fine for Amazon's advertising targeting system violating GDPR consent and transparency requirements. Amazon contested the fine.

violation_type: Facial recognition tag suggestions without BIPA consent
outcome: Settlement
summary: BIPA class action over Facebook's Tag Suggestions feature using facial recognition without Illinois users' consent; settled for $650 million — the largest privacy class action settlement in US history at the time.
